regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality test is whether it survives decomposition. IIP at 6.7% YoY (down from 8.8%) and core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) suggest the industrial engine is losing torque even as the PMI composite at 54.6 — an 83rd-percentile print — holds up on services momentum. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the one number that earns optimism: it is 180bps above last month and approaching the 78-80% threshold historically associated with private capex commitments. The inversion: if services PMI is doing the heavy lifting while manufacturing PMI slips to 52.8 (down from 53.5), this is a consumption-led expansion with a capex story layered on top — not the broad-based industrial recovery the budget arithmetic requires.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% is above the RBI's midpoint, but the decomposition is where the danger lives. Food at 5.52% is noisy and seasonal; core CPI at 3.9% is the number RBI actually watches — and at a 28th percentile, it is not the problem. Fuel inflation at 22.93% — a 95th-percentile print, up from 20.05% — is the structural threat: it feeds into WPI at 9.92%, compresses manufacturer margins before they can pass through, and eventually surfaces in core CPI with a two-quarter lag. RBI's own inflation forecast just moved to 5.1% from 4.6% — a 50bps revision that the repo rate at 5.25% has not yet acknowledged.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — is the structural fault line. CD ratio at 81.4% has eased one month from 82.5% but remains at a 75th-percentile elevation; the relief is arithmetic, not structural. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that wholesale funding dependency is rising as retail deposits lag — the classic pre-stress pattern. The last time India's CD ratio sustained above 80% during a rate-cut cycle was FY14; within four quarters, the taper tantrum forced 75bps of emergency hikes. Today's FX reserves are $100bn higher, but the funding structure is no less fragile.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% against CPI at 4.45% and RBI's own forecast at 5.1% leaves a real rate of approximately 15bps — thin enough to be irrelevant as an anchor. With INR at a 91st-percentile 96.15 and US 10Y at 5.01%, the carry differential that attracts FII equity flows is not the problem; the carry differential that governs debt flows and corporate hedging costs is. A rate cut from here would compress that differential further, accelerating INR weakness and importing the fuel inflation that is already at a decade-high. RBI is not cutting — the question is whether it is forced to hike.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY is the strongest single number in today's data set, and capacity utilisation at 77.4% provides the demand-pull rationale. Private capex historically accelerates when utilisation crosses 78-80%; at 77.4%, India is one quarter away from that threshold if the trend holds. The inversion: core sector at 5.4% (moderating from 6.0%) and IIP overall at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) suggest the capital goods surge is concentrated in specific sub-sectors — likely defence, electronics, and PLI-linked manufacturing — rather than broad-based industrial investment. Cement and steel dispatch data would confirm or deny; absent that, the capex story is real but narrower than the headline implies.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is a 71st-percentile print and a sharp jump from ₹1,74,116 crore — but September collections always carry advance filing effects from the prior quarter, which can inflate the month by 15-20%. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% are the cleaner signal: two-wheelers are the informal economy's consumption barometer, and 19.7% growth suggests rural and semi-urban demand is genuinely recovering, not just urban discretionary. The tension: credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%, a 26th-percentile low) suggests urban consumers are either deleveraging or hitting credit limits — a quiet warning beneath the vehicle sales headline.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding dependency rising as retail deposits lag.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from weaker peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 to ease deposit pressure, but transmission will be uneven. Position for credit quality divergence: large-cap banks outperform mid-cap lenders.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either RBI rate cuts or NBFC stress. Last time this divergence persisted (2022), smaller lenders faced funding crunches within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up 180bps from 75.6% prior month). Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY, moderating but still positive. India GDP FY estimate at 7.7% (80th percentile hi), RBI GDP forecast at 6.7% (76th percentile mid). PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile hi), services PMI at 54.5 — both signalling sustained demand.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, industrial machinery, and cement stocks. Infrastructure plays (roads, ports, power) will see order book expansion through Q3. Avoid consumer discretionary — capex is crowding out consumption. Allocate to EPC contractors and equipment lessors; they'll see 18-24 month order visibility. Expect margin pressure in Q2 due to input cost inflation (WPI at 9.92%, fuel at 22.93%), but volume growth will offset.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the 74th percentile — historically, this level precedes 12-18 months of sustained capex. Last similar reading (2021) led to 22% IIP capgoods growth over the following year.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Retail Equity Inflows Hit Record Highs","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (rising 2 consecutive months: 29,845→31,961→32,297). SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (93rd percentile hi, rising 2 in a row). MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile hi, rising 2 in a row). DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile hi, rising 2 in a row). SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (82nd percentile hi).","implication":"Retail equity flows are structural, not cyclical. Overweight mid-cap and small-cap indices — SIP money is chasing growth, not value. Avoid high-dividend, low-growth stocks; they'll underperform as SIP AUM compounds into growth assets. Watch for SIP account growth (100.18 Cr) vs SIP AUM growth (18.62 Tr) — average ticket size rising 25% YoY signals affluent money entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour; lock in gains in overvalued segments.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile and rising 2 consecutive months is a 10-year high. Historically, such peaks have preceded 8-12% market corrections within 6-9 months as retail euphoria peaks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% prior month, 95th percentile hi). WPI at 9.92% (up from 9.78%, 67th percentile mid). Brent crude at $96.22/bbl (flat, 68th percentile mid). Iron ore at $161.91/tonne (up from $97.57, 63rd percentile mid). Copper at $6.805/lb (82nd percentile hi, rising 3 of last 5 months).","implication":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a structural headwind for transport, power, and manufacturing. Underweight airlines, logistics, and cement — margin compression will be severe in Q2-Q3. Overweight energy stocks (oil, gas, coal) and commodity exporters; they'll benefit from input cost pass-through. RBI will struggle to cut rates while fuel inflation remains elevated; expect repo rate to stay at 5.25% through Q2. Hedge CAD risk — oil imports will spike India's current account deficit.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 10-year extreme. Last time fuel inflation exceeded 20% (2022), it persisted for 8+ months and forced RBI to hike rates, not cut.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"US Rates Sticky, Carry Trades Unwind Risk","data_text":"US 10Y Treasury at 5.01% (91st percentile hi, up 4 of last 5 months: 4.95→4.96→4.97→5.00→5.01). Fed funds rate at 3.63% (67th percentile mid, flat). Fed balance sheet at $6,746.5B (rising 3 in a row: 6,675→6,737→6,740→6,746). BOJ rate at 1.0% (86th percentile hi, up from 0.75%). US core CPI at 2.45% (falling 2 in a row: 2.5→2.47→2.45).","implication":"US rates are sticky at 5%+ despite cooling core CPI — Fed is in no rush to cut. This kills carry trades (borrow USD at 3.6%, invest in INR at 5.25%). Expect INR weakness to persist; RBI will defend at 96.50 but won't intervene aggressively. Overweight USD-denominated assets; DXY will likely test 101-102 by Q3. Avoid emerging market debt — carry unwind will force capital repatriation. BOJ's rate hike to 1% is a tail risk for yen carry trades; watch for sudden yen strength.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 91st percentile and rising 4 of last 5 months is a 10-year high. Last time 10Y yields were this elevated (2023), they stayed above 4.5% for 6+ months, crushing EM flows.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates Despite RBI Defence","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.81, 91st percentile hi, rising 3 of last 5 months: 95.24→96.15→95.24→94.34→95.24→96.15). India VIX at 11.248 (6th percentile lo, down from 11.39, falling 2 of last 5 months). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile hi, up 1 of last 2: -114→-3,111→29,631). US VIX at 14.87 (8th percentile lo, flat).","implication":"INR is weakening despite strong FII inflows — this signals structural capital outflow pressure (likely debt repatriation as US rates stay high). RBI will defend at 96.50 but cannot hold indefinitely without burning reserves. Overweight USD hedges for corporates with INR liabilities. Avoid INR-denominated bonds; yields won't compensate for currency depreciation. Watch FII flows closely — if they reverse, INR will break 97 within weeks. India's CAD will widen due to oil imports + INR weakness; expect RBI to tighten liquidity in Q2.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 96.15 is at 91st percentile weakness. Last time INR weakened this sharply (2022), it took 4 months to stabilise and required RBI rate hikes + FX intervention.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Decoupling From IT Stock Proxy","data_text":"Office absorption at 29.9 Mn sqft (24th percentile lo, up from 28.2 prior month, rising 3 of last 5: 26.9→48→29.9→21.5→26.9→48). Office vacancy at 13.9% (38th percentile lo, down from 17.2, falling 2 of last 5). Nifty IT index flat YTD despite office absorption strength. GCC (Global Capability Centre) leasing now 35%+ of total office absorption vs 15% five years ago. Rent growth in Bengaluru at 100.6 (57th percentile mid, up from 94).","implication":"Traditional IT services are NOT the office buyer anymore — GCCs (captive centres of MNCs) are. This means office RE is decoupling from Nifty IT as a proxy. Overweight commercial real estate (Embassy, Mindspace) and office landlords; they're capturing GCC demand, not IT services churn. Underweight Nifty IT — the sector is shedding office space (WFH, automation) while GCCs are absorbing it. This is a 2-3 year structural shift: office RE will outperform IT stocks. Falsifiable: if GCC leasing drops below 30% of absorption in next 2 quarters, thesis breaks.","pct_10y":24,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 24th percentile is historically weak, but the composition shift (GCC dominance) is a 10-year structural change. Last time office demand was this weak (2020), it was driven by IT services contraction; today it's driven by IT services consolidation + GCC expansion.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with PMI composite at 54.6 and IIP capital goods at 16.1% presents a coherent expansion narrative — until you notice that IIP overall has decelerated to 6.7% from 8.8% and core sector to 5.4% from 6.0%, suggesting the industrial base is narrowing even as the investment cycle headline strengthens. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up 180bps in a single month — is the most credible forward indicator for private capex commitment, sitting one quarter away from the 78-80% threshold that historically triggers balance-sheet investment decisions. Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY confirm that the informal economy is participating in this expansion, not just the formal corporate sector captured by GST. Credit card growth at 2.3% — a 26th-percentile low, down from 5.6% — is the single data point that does not fit the consumption optimism, and it deserves more attention than it is getting.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Euro Stoxx 50 at a 100th-percentile 6,318 and US PMI composite at 56 — an 84th-percentile print, up from 54.5 — are pricing a global growth re-acceleration that US 10Y at 5.01% simultaneously prices as structurally inflationary. US GDP SAAR has decelerated to 1.5% from 2.1%, yet equities are at all-time highs and PMI is expanding — a divergence that resolves either through earnings disappointment or through a bond market that is simply wrong about the terminal rate. China at 4.3% GDP (down from 5.0%) with composite PMI at 49.5 remains the deflationary anchor in the global system, keeping commodity prices from a full breakout despite Brent at $96.22. BOJ at 1.0% — a 25bps hike from 0.75% — is the structural shift that matters most for global carry: every basis point of Japanese rate normalisation tightens global dollar liquidity by unwinding yen-funded positions.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 crore — a 100th-percentile print, rising for two consecutive months from ₹8,930 crore — is the most important domestic liquidity fact of the week, and it is being funded by SIP inflows at a record ₹32,297 crore with SIP AUM crossing ₹18.62 trillion. FII equity net at ₹29,631 crore has swung sharply positive from -₹3,112 crore prior month, but the trend data shows this is a single-month reversal, not a sustained re-entry — the sequence reads -114 → -3,112 → 29,631, which is a bounce, not a regime change. Bank credit at 17.1% against deposits at 10.8% means the banking system is funding incremental credit growth through wholesale markets and CD issuances, not through deposit mobilisation — a structurally fragile arrangement when US 10Y is at 5.01% and global risk appetite can reverse. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 crore is at a 0th-percentile low, suggesting corporates are not yet tapping capital markets to bridge the funding gap — they are relying on bank credit, which tightens the CD ratio further.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty at 23,414 (75th percentile) and Bank Nifty at 56,471 (93rd percentile) are pricing an earnings cycle that fuel inflation at 22.93% and WPI at 9.92% will test in the next two quarters — margin compression in industrials and consumer staples is the arithmetic consequence, not a tail risk. Office absorption at 29.9 million sqft with vacancy falling to 13.9% from 17.2% tells a structurally positive commercial real estate story, but the REIT prices are telling the opposite: Embassy REIT down to ₹369.92 from ₹441.07, Mindspace to ₹345.06 from ₹505.58 — the market is discounting the asset class against a US 10Y at 5.01% that makes the yield spread unattractive. GCC leasing at 35%+ of total office absorption (vs 15% five years ago) is the structural shift that the REIT derating is ignoring: this is not cyclical IT demand but sovereign-grade corporate infrastructure investment that does not vacate on a hiring freeze. Residential real estate shows unsold inventory at 616,000 units rising while sales at 90,715 units fall — affordability at a 19th-percentile index of 3.5 with home loan rates at 7.85% is the binding constraint.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Ranked by probability × impact: first, fuel inflation at 22.93% feeding into core CPI with a two-quarter lag — if core moves from 3.9% toward 4.5%, the RBI's extended pause becomes a forced hike, repricing every rate-sensitive asset simultaneously. Second, the credit-deposit divergence at 630bps — if deposit growth does not accelerate to 13-14% within two quarters, the RBI's macro-prudential toolkit (risk weights, LCR tightening) becomes the next policy lever, and NBFC credit at 14.9% is the first casualty. Third, US 10Y at 5.01% with Fed funds at 3.63% — the inverted logic of a steepening curve in a slowing economy (US GDP SAAR at 1.5%) suggests either a fiscal premium being priced or a growth re-acceleration; either resolution is disruptive for EM flows. Fourth, INR at 96.15 with Brent flat at $96.22 — any crude spike above $100 widens CAD by 40bps per $10 increment and forces RBI FX intervention that draws down reserves. Watch Thursday's US core PCE print at 3.34% — if it moves above 3.5%, the Fed's pause narrative breaks and every EM carry trade unwinds simultaneously.

"}
